Ok, I think I know the issue, which is very similar to another flaky test fixed in the past. 

The issue is when we shift the fake clock with `manager.clock.Sleep` during `AddAfter` (invoked by `AddRateLimited`), which processes the pending queue (`waitingForQueue`) asynchronously. More details on the similar past issue: (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114944#discussion_r1069179801). I was able to repro this manually by inserting short real-clock sleeps like here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119506/commits/cd563d8c285ba73379cc9680e57b614e98c8e10b

I think the issue was introduced actually here by the use of fake clock: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/8ed23558b44bed8ce60f4171ea0a87739221110c. This commit was added to master after 1.27 so no need for cherry-picking the fix.

I think the fix is to call `awaitForQueueLen` instead of `manager.clock.Sleep(fastJobApiBackoff)`, because it repeatedly shifts the fake clock after `waitingForQueue` is processed.

review_comments: Just to confirm: NumRequeues doesn't depend on AddAfter, correct?

Yes, the `NumRequeues` is computed based on the `failures` counter in the rate limiter: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/util/workqueue/default_rate_limiters.go#L110-L114. 

This counter is bumped when calling `when`, before `AddAfter` is called: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4e8908d56671c1bae588151d1d2fcbd4fa56b049/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/util/workqueue/rate_limiting_queue.go#L110C39-L110C50.

This is why the `if` passes consistently, while the item may never really reach the actual queue, due to the race condition when using `AddAfter` with fake clocks.
